title: Mexico Reports 52 Percent Reduction in Homicides; September Registers Lowest for That Month Since 2015
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [October 13, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/sesnsp-reporta-
reduccion-de-52-por-ciento-en-homicidios-septiembre-registra-minimo-para-ese-
mes-desde-2015/), Mexico's leading investigative journalism magazine._

The daily average of **intentional homicides** in Mexico decreased by **52
percent** between September 2024 and September 2026, as reported by **Marcela
Figueroa Franco** , head of the **Executive Secretariat of the National Public
Security System**. The official presented a decrease from 86.9 to 42.2
homicides per day, equivalent to approximately **45 fewer intentional
homicides per day**.

While presenting the results of the **National Public Security Strategy**
during the presidential press conference on October 13, led by Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo, she highlighted that **September 2026 registered the lowest
daily average of intentional homicides** for that month since 2015, according
to national records.

Regarding territorial distribution, the Executive Secretariat of the National
Public Security System (SESNSP) reported that **seven states concentrated
nearly half of the intentional homicides registered in the country between
January and September 2026**.

**Baja California** topped the list, with 8.5 percent of the national total,
followed by **Guanajuato** , also with 8.5 percent, although with three fewer
homicides than the first state. In third place was **Chihuahua** , with 7.8
percent, while Sinaloa concentrated 7.7 percent.

The **State of Mexico** was in fifth position, with 6.4 percent of the
national total; **Guerrero** , sixth, with 5.7 percent, and **Morelos** ,
seventh, with 5.2 percent.

For his part, the head of the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection,
**Omar García Harfuch** , reported that, as part of the federal strategy,
between October 1, 2024 and September 30, 2026, **more than 70,500 people were
arrested for their alleged participation in high-impact crimes**.

During that period, security forces seized **36,300 firearms** and **569 tons
of drugs**. Among the seizures, more than two tons of fentanyl and 9,553,000
pills of this substance were reported.

The secretary also reported that the Mexican Army and the Secretariat of the
Navy **disabled 2,792 clandestine laboratories and concentration areas** used
for the production of synthetic drugs in 24 states.

In the fight against **cocaine** trafficking, García Harfuch highlighted the
strengthening of the Secretariat of the Navy’s maritime surveillance
operations, through which more than 93 tons of this drug have been seized.

Another of the crimes addressed during the presentation was **extortion**. The
official noted that, since the implementation of the National Strategy against
Extortion on July 6, 2025, and until September 30, 2026, **2,170 people
allegedly related to this crime** were arrested in 24 states of the country.

According to García Harfuch, these actions seek to stop threats, the
collection of protection payments, and other forms of extortion against
merchants, transporters, and producers.
